verdict.line: You win the lane and the kill window every time you open with E, but she claws the overall number back to 48.9% by surviving on A Thousand Cuts and disengaging through W.

brief.thesis: Irelia's whole kill pattern runs through E (Flawless Duet): land the stun-and-mark and Bladesurge becomes a free, healing dash that can refresh itself off the Mark, which is why lane advantage and solo-kill advantage both sit with Irelia despite a 48.9% head-to-head over 585 games. The counterweight is Gwen's W (Hallowed Mist) — it blocks your single-target Q from ever selecting her once she commits to it, so an all-in without an E stun first can simply whiff. Her passive, A Thousand Cuts, also scales off your current health and heals her on champion hits, so grinding auto-trades quietly favor her even though her own poke (Q, Snip Snip!) is short-range and committal.

theirWindow.what: Once Hallowed Mist is up she can't be targeted from outside it, so a Bladesurge thrown at her now will fail to lock on — back off, let the 22-18s cooldown run, and only commit your real all-in once it's down or you've already stepped inside it.

yourWindow.when: Your E lands and marks her
yourWindow.what: Chain Q (Bladesurge) onto the stunned, Marked Gwen immediately — it heals you, refreshes its own cooldown off the Mark, and stacks Ionian Fervor attack speed for everything that follows.

start.why: Measured as the dominant start (51.4% over 584 games, 83.3% pick) — the sustain and early damage let you force trades before she has Skip 'n Slash online at rank 2.

boots.why: 48.9% over 372 games, 59% pick — magic resist blunts her passive's on-hit damage and Q's true-damage center hit still gets through regardless, so the tenacity against Needlework's slow matters more than armor here.

core.why: Highest-winning core start (58.9% over 107 games with this full path) — current-health on-hit damage trades evenly with her own max-health passive instead of losing the race to it.
Keeps your on-hit and attack-speed scaling climbing while giving you a split-push answer to her own splitpush threat.
Magic resist plus more on-hit damage directly undercuts A Thousand Cuts and her magic-infused autos after Skip 'n Slash.

the game runs long and her splitpush plus ranged Needlework poke starts punishing you for playing alone

runes.keystoneWhy: Measured as the top page (55.8%, 34.9% pick) — the stacking adaptive force and sustain give you the staying power to out-trade a passive that heals her every time she hits you.

summoners.why: Flash + Ignite is the measured standard (51% win rate, 88.1% pick) — Ignite's steady damage eats into the health percentage her passive would otherwise heal back; Exhaust is the alternative (39.3%, 8.1% pick) when you'd rather shut down her Skip 'n Slash attack-speed window than secure a kill.

playing.title: Open every trade with E
playing.detail: Never Q first — Flawless Duet's stun and Mark turn Bladesurge into a free, self-healing dash that can refresh itself if she's still Marked or dies to it.

playing.title: Force her W before you all-in
playing.detail: Poke until Hallowed Mist is burned defensively or track its 22-18s cooldown, since a Bladesurge thrown at her while the mist is up simply can't find a target from outside it.

playing.title: Avoid extended auto trades
playing.detail: A Thousand Cuts deals bonus magic damage based on your current health and heals her on every champion hit, so long back-and-forth exchanges bleed you faster than her — win with burst and disengage instead.

playing.title: Track her E dash timer
playing.detail: Skip 'n Slash (13 down to 11s cooldown) grants attack speed, range and magic on-hit for a few seconds after she uses it — that's her short all-in window, and it only partially refunds if she whiffs.

playing.title: Don't rely on W for her damage
playing.detail: Defiant Dance only reduces physical damage, and Snip Snip's true-damage center hit plus her on-hit magic ignore it entirely — charge it to tank autoattacks, not to block her real burst.

playing.title: Chain Q off your R's Mark
playing.detail: From level 6 on, Vanguard's Edge marks anyone it explodes on, so following an ult hit with Q refreshes Bladesurge and keeps you dashing while Ionian Fervor stacks climb.

playing.title: Respect Needlework's range post-6
playing.detail: Her ult reaches 1200 range and can be cast up to two more times — don't greed CS or overextend past minions once she hits level 6 without accounting for that long slow-and-poke.

brief.patchCaveat: Win rates, build order, runes, and summoner spells above are measured from live OP.GG games on the current patch; the mechanical reasoning and timing calls are my own tactical read, not measured data.
